newsitem.title: UK: NWE spot gas oil weaker but buyers stay sidelined.
newsitem.headline: NWE spot gas oil weaker but buyers stay sidelined.

text.p: NWE spot gas oil prices were slightly weaker in early trade on Friday with IPE gas oil moving lower in correction to Thursday's gains and slack buying interest putting barge and cargo premiums under pressure.
Brokers said the strong dollar versus the mark and Thursday sharply higher IPE have pegged buyers firmly to the sidelines, helping to balance tight prompt supply.
"Despite the tightish prompt (barge) supply only sellers are left for July -- they would do 50 cents (over August IPE) if the buyers were there", one barge broker said.

Prompt and early August lifting barges were assessed flat with buying notionally around Aug evens to +25 cents and selling at 50 cents to +$1 fob ARA. Storage material was valued 50 cents to $1 under refinery oil.
Diesel barge premiums eased 50 cents to Aug +$4/$5 fob ARA.

The relaxed of buying interest and currently good supply coming out of Ventspils put 0.2 sulphur cargo premiums under pressure, wiping out the small backwardation between prompt and early August deliveries.
Prompt and early August deliveries talked flat at Aug IPE +50 cents/+$1 per tonne the prompt market easing 50 cents.
Diesel cargo premiums were more stable with fairly busy trade this week taking out any surplus.
Prompt deliveries talked Aug IPE +$4/+$5 with Aug 1-15 cargoes at Aug IPE +$4.50/+$5 and Aug 16-31 at Sep IPE +$4.50/+$5 a tonne cif NWE.
